# SOW Spec — Wds_project (standalone-app, new build)

## Project Summary

Wds_project is a new-build `standalone-app` (custom web application, "Standalone Task & Approval Management") built with a Next.js / React / TypeScript frontend, Node.js / Express / TypeScript backend, PostgreSQL via Prisma) at the `basic` plan tier. The attached Technical SOW classifies it as an internal pilot / proof of concept that validates the WebDesk Node.js development skill end to end. There is no existing website. Total scope: 749 hours / $56,175 USD across 9 sprints and 5 milestones, 2026-10-12 to 2026-12-09 (43 working days). The pilot runs locally on Docker only, with no production deployment.

Design deliverable per D-DES-01 is HTML mockups with revision caps of 5 (homepage) and 3 (other pages); see **Open Items** because the estimation sheet carries no mockup hours. All client communication routes through Hazel (Internal PM). The FLAG-004 blocklist is captured in frontmatter.

## Technical Baseline

Source: attached Technical SOW (`Nodejs_Custom_-app_Technical_Statement_of_Work_SOW.docx`, dated 2026-10-09). Read it in full at G0; the points below are the ones that shape planning.

| Layer | Technology |
|-------|-----------|
| Frontend | Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS |
| Backend | Node.js, Express.js, TypeScript (REST APIs), Zod validation |
| Database | PostgreSQL with Prisma (schema and migrations) |
| Authentication | Secure server-managed session-based authentication |
| Testing | Vitest (unit, integration), Playwright (end-to-end) |
| Local execution | Docker / Docker Compose, Git |
| Notifications | In-app (PostgreSQL) + email through a free-tier transactional provider (Brevo suggested) behind a replaceable provider interface |

**Application roles and pilot accounts.** Three application roles: Administrator, Manager, Employee. Hazel receives the Manager role as Project Manager. AS receives the Manager role with designated-reviewer responsibility; the backend must validate reviewer identity so that not every Manager can approve. Accounts for Administrator, Hazel and AS are created through a documented setup process with no hardcoded passwords in committed source.

**Rules that must hold.** Permissions and workflow rules are enforced on the backend. Only the Administrator changes allocated time, and allocated time is planned time, not time worked. Audit entries are append-only. Rejection is recorded as an approval decision and does not add a Rejected status; the task stays In Review. Kanban moves call the same transition validation as normal actions. Email failures must not undo task or approval changes.

**Requirement ID ranges in the Technical SOW.** FR-001 to FR-097, TR-001 to TR-020, DATA-001 to DATA-012, UX-001 to UX-012, SEC-001 to SEC-010, QA-001 to QA-014. Sixteen functional acceptance criteria are listed under "Functional Acceptance Criteria".

**Deployment boundary.** Local Docker operation is sufficient. No production hosting, public domain, load balancing or autoscaling (Plan Summary: "Excluded: Production hosting, paid SMS, advanced enterprise infrastructure").

## Risks & Assumptions

### Assumptions
- The plan starts 2026-10-12 and ends 2026-12-09, weekdays only; no weekend work is scheduled.
- Three engineers are available in parallel; the peak Sprint 3 (113 hours in 5 working days) depends on it (Plan Summary note).
- Frontend and backend work proceeds in parallel after API contracts are agreed in Sprint 1.
- Email notifications need a free-provider account and verified sender; in-app notifications are testable independently.
- All estimates are planning forecasts, not verified actuals.

### Risks
- **Thin defect buffer (High)**: only 24 hours of dedicated defect resolution and retest (Task #16.2), 3.2% of 749 hours, with the last sprint running 52 hours in 3 working days. Any slip in earlier sprints lands on the 2026-12-09 date.
- **Peak-sprint staffing (Medium)**: Sprint 3 carries 113 hours in one week and needs all three engineers; one absence breaks the sprint.
- **Fixed-price exposure (Medium)**: if the engagement is priced as fixed (the default SOW basis), overrun is absorbed by WebDesk. Pricing basis was not stated in the intake.
- **Undefined behaviours (Medium)**: reminder timing, post-rejection follow-up and mandatory time-change reason are open (see Required From Client).
- **Email provider restrictions (Low)**: free-tier limits and account verification may delay real email delivery testing.

### Open Items
1. **Mockup hours are not in the estimate.** Intake commits to HTML mockups (5 homepage / 3 other-page revisions) and G2 mockup sign-off. The estimation sheet contains no mockup production hours: Task #3.1 (12 h) is the app UX shell, noted "Pilot UI; no approved mockup", and the Technical SOW states "no separate client design-approval phase is required". Sales chose on 2026-10-09 to keep the HTML mockup commitment. Hours stay at 749 and cost at $56,175 until the sheet is revised. At G0, confirm with the Internal PM whether a mockup phase is added (this needs a revised estimate) before G2 is scheduled.
2. **"Homepage" is undefined.** The app has no marketing homepage. Confirm which screen counts as the homepage for the 5-revision cap (Login or Dashboard are the candidates).
3. **Pricing basis** (fixed vs hourly) is not stated; $75/hr is implied by 56,175 / 749 and was confirmed for internal use.
4. **Role assignment check.** Intake lists BD as designer and AS as dev lead. AS is also the in-app reviewer persona in the Technical SOW. Recorded as given.

### Pre-flight gates
- G0 intake gate
- G0.5 audit gate
- G1 plan gate
- G2 design gate
- G3 scaffold gate
- G4 sprint QA
- G5 milestone gate
- G6 pre-launch (for this project, "launch" means the local handoff: no production deployment)

Gate content for `standalone-app` is defined by `nodejs/projects/standalone-app/gates.md`.
